parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the task as a clean-room reimplementation of gron from CLI behavior and bundled docs, with no source-code lookup or binary analysis allowed.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent inspected the workspace and docs, chose Go because Go 1.21 was available, then delegated six distinct behavioral probe areas to a swarm while retaining the later implementation path itself.
parallel.implementation: No replacement implementation was written. The completed child work consisted of probe reports under /tmp/probe for forward rendering, modes, CLI/URL behavior, and color behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent received a swarm aggregate with four completed and two aborted children, but did not assemble findings into source, compile.sh, or a deliverable executable before packaging.
parallel.verification: The parallel run performed many behavior probes against the reference executable, but no verifier checked a produced implementation because none existed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The ungron and sort/order probe scopes were aborted, the implementation never started, and the official artifact contained only original repository files and the reference executable.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room gron reimplementation requirement and used only local behavioral probes plus bundled documentation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent owned all work, made a TodoList covering probing, implementation, diff testing, and compile.sh, and did not delegate to subagents.
serial.implementation: No replacement implementation was written. The serial agent stayed in exploratory probing of forward, ungron, values, stream, json, colors, URL, and parser edge cases.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because there were no components or child reports, there was no integration step; the submitted artifact still contained only the original workspace files.
serial.verification: The serial run compared many individual observations against the reference binary but never produced or tested a candidate implementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run was cancelled during probing before implementation, diff-test harness work, compile script creation, or final build verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room behavioral reimplementation task and the restrictions against source lookup, wrapping, and binary analysis.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and followed the same prompt, also treating the task as behavioral reverse engineering of gron.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the outcome; both understood the task but neither delivered implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed behavior discovery into six swarm children after the parent selected Go as an implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one main agent, no subagents, and a local todo plan for probing, implementation, testing, and compile.sh.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel externalized probe ownership to children and then had child failure boundaries; serial kept ownership local and had no child boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included shared known facts and scoped behavior areas; no cross-agent implementation interface was established because children were probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried the task context in one main trajectory and did not need handoff or interface contracts between agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete context difference is the presence of parallel child handoff boundaries, but there is no directly evidenced missing brief or incompatible interface contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified Go 1.21 as available and suitable but shifted into delegated probing rather than creating files for a Go implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also identified Go 1.21 as available and continued designing behavior from probes but did not create implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on Go but neither materialized source; parallel differed by waiting on child reports while serial continued one-agent probing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The swarm returned an aggregate result reporting four completed children and two aborted children, and the parent did not act on the aborted scopes before closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; its main trajectory was cancelled while still probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel has a failed-child result lifecycle with no takeover, while serial has ordinary single-agent cancellation without a delegated result boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote probe reports in /tmp/probe, but no source tree integration or final workspace implementation write occurred.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made no implementation writes or integrations; the artifact likewise contained only original files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no shared-state collision or integration conflict; both lacked final implementation artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel collected behavior probes, but official evaluation reported compile_failed with all 233 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial collected local behavior observations, but official evaluation also reported compile_failed with all 233 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No evaluator-aligned verification of a candidate implementation occurred in either mode; official acceptance failures match.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after the swarm work, with child cancellations and no remaining parent implementation step.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out after extended local probing, without starting implementation or packaging a buildable solution.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget before implementation; parallel's distinctive budget consequence was unrecovered aborted child scope.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both modes failed with compile_failed and 0/233 test quality. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel delegated required behavior discovery to six children and left two aborted scopes untaken over, while serial stayed in one local trajectory and was cancelled during probing. Since neither run produced a buildable replacement, the retained parallel pattern is adverse but not an explanation for an outcome split.
parallel_contributors: Six-way delegated probing produced four usable reports but left ungron and sort/order scopes aborted without parent takeover.
The parent did not convert returned probe findings into source files, compile.sh, or a candidate executable before closure.
serial_contributors: The single serial agent continued direct probing and planning until cancellation, without a child boundary or handoff failure.
Serial likewise failed to create source, compile.sh, or a buildable replacement executable.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Neither run reached implementation, so no ordinary coding defect or partial implementation difference separates the official outcomes.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel adverse process event

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly intended to implement in Go after probing; the failure was not absence of an implementation owner but failure to recover aborted delegated scopes before implementation.
No multiple component implementations were produced, so there was no concrete unowned integration object.
There was no completed component set or candidate deliverable waiting for an unowned final assembly step.
The parent owned the overall transition from probes to implementation; the breakdown was later failure takeover, not missing pipeline ownership.
No single mandatory preflight harness or oracle gate blocked otherwise parallel implementation work; the children performed concurrent behavioral probes.
Although most child work was investigative, the investigation phase did not complete cleanly and the direct adverse boundary was aborted child scopes without takeover.
The implementation path started too late, but the directly evidenced boundary is unrecovered child failure rather than a separate capacity allocation episode.
The six-child fan-out and timeout are visible, but breadth alone is not retained because the same chain is more specifically the parent failing to take over aborted required scopes.
No single child assignment is proven to be uniquely overbroad relative to siblings; two children were aborted as part of the same closure chain.
The child briefs included scoped behavior areas and known global facts; no already-known task or acceptance requirement is shown missing from a brief and causing unusable work.
The children were probe reporters, not separately implemented components expected to interoperate, and no incompatible interface work was produced.
No known finding is shown present before transfer and absent afterward; the failure is not repeated work caused by lost context.
Some completed probe summaries were long, but there is no direct evidence that their size or structure prevented reduction before an otherwise actionable decision.
No returned child information described a superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent consumed to make a stale action.
The completed child summaries do not show incompatible reports that reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at an integration decision.
The parent never made an observable whole-task completion or acceptance decision based on partial artifacts; it timed out with no implementation.
There was no replacement child or retry attempt that repeated work without inherited findings or workspace state.
